findings.title: `schema-conformance.home-vacated` fires on pre-jigc history — a stock brownfield repo is red at exit 1 the moment `jigc setup` runs, with no exit that clears it
findings.location: crates/cli/src/orphan.rs:579-595 (`vacated_homes`, the `git_path_has_history` leg) · crates/cli/src/cli.rs:1516 (store-sweep call site) · crates/cli/src/render.rs:1212 (`STORE_EXIT_FLIPS` membership)
findings.evidence:
Increment 7's own deliverable is *"a declared home **jigc committed into** that is now empty"* (implementation/roadmap.md → Milestone 52 Increment 7), but the shipped predicate is `!occupied && git_path_has_history(repo_root, &home.path)` (orphan.rs:593) — any history at the path, with no discriminator for whether jigc ever wrote there. The producer's own doc-comment states this: *"It does not claim jigc wrote what the history carries."* That is the exact gap M51's completion-audit HIGH closed one check over (`orphaned-instance` was narrowed to `orphan::Territory` because the stamp is un-namespaced); this check ships with no such discriminator on the history leg.

DRIVEN (debug binary at HEAD, `dev/jigc-rig bare`):
  rig=$(dev/jigc-rig bare) || exit; eval "$rig"; cd "$REPO"
  printf '# Changelog\n\n## 0.1.0\n' > CHANGELOG.md && git add CHANGELOG.md && git commit -qm 'add changelog'
  git rm -q CHANGELOG.md && git commit -qm 'drop changelog'
  "$JIGC" setup >/dev/null   # exit 0
  "$JIGC" validate           # exit 1
→ `blocking · schema-conformance.home-vacated — 'changelog' homes its one document at 'CHANGELOG.md' … nothing is there now`, and the sweep's trailer says it "exits non-zero rather than report a green". Nothing in that repository was ever managed by jigc.

IT IS A REGRESSION, MEASURED: on the identical tree the installed `~/.local/bin/jigc` (1.0.0-rc.15, the wave's own base version) answers `no findings — the committed store validates clean`, exit 0.

NO EXIT CLEARS IT. Driven on the same tree: `jigc unmanage CHANGELOG.md` → `no-op: CHANGELOG.md is not managed (nothing to drop)`, exit 0, and `jigc validate` still exits 1. `jigc ingest` classifies nothing at that path. The route's remaining exit — *"retiring `changelog` for good means taking the pack that declares this home out of the composition"* — is unavailable for `changelog`, which is an **embedded** dev-pack doctype, and a project-layer schema shadow that moved its `placement:` would trip the M38/M49 freeze assert (location is inside `schema-hash`). The only act that clears it is re-creating a file the adopter deliberately deleted.

CLASS, AND HOW THE COUNT WAS DERIVED: the subject is `orphan::fixed_identity_homes` over the resolved schemas — every doctype whose `Schema::projection()` is `IdentityKind::Fixed` with a home path. `grep -rln "placement:\|singleton: true" crates/cli/pack/schemas/ packs/methodology/schemas/` → **5 files**: `changelog` (CHANGELOG.md), `vision` (VISION.md), `roadmap` (docs/roadmap.md), `decisions-log` (docs/decisions-log.md), `deferral-ledger` (docs/deferral-ledger.md). Both packs compose by default (`jigc start` header: `Pack: dev/… | methodology/…`). **3 of the 5 driven to a live fire** in one bare repo by committing and then `git rm`-ing `CHANGELOG.md`, `VISION.md` and `docs/roadmap.md`: two `home-vacated` rows plus the changelog run above, `jigc validate` exit 1 each time. The remaining 2 differ from these only in the path string.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT (fixture-topology masking): all four arms of `crates/cli/tests/home_vacated.rs` build `State::CommittedSingletons` (`grep -n "State::" crates/cli/tests/home_vacated.rs` → 4 hits, all `CommittedSingletons`) — an **adopted** corpus whose docs jigc itself committed. The never-adopted corpus is structurally unreachable from the Rust suites: `grep -rn "State::Bare" crates/cli/tests/` → **0 hits** (`bare` is rig-only, per `RIG_ONLY_STATES`). So the suite certifies the wave's designed cell (`git mv CHANGELOG.md HISTORY.md` on a jigc-managed corpus) and is blind to the dominant real-world shape, `jigc setup` on a repo with ordinary pre-jigc history.

Full gate is green over this (3785 passed / 0 failed), which is the point: the defect is outside every fixture the suite can build.

findings.title: The `home-vacated` route's locator names nothing on an uncommitted deletion, and the repair it prescribes is not the one that state needs
findings.evidence:
`vacated_homes`' emptiness leg reads the **worktree** (`engine::index::committed_instances` asks `path.exists()`, index.rs:789), so an *uncommitted* `rm` of a placement doc satisfies it. Its own doc-comment acknowledges the cell (*"the uncommitted-deletion case is additionally adjudicated by the file-state gate"*), but the route it prints was written for the committed-removal cell only.

DRIVEN (debug binary at HEAD):
  rig=$(dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons) || exit; eval "$rig"; cd "$REPO"
  rm CHANGELOG.md
  "$JIGC" validate   # exit 1
→ two blocking rows for one act:
   `blocking (gates at finalize) · reconciliation.rename — tracked managed doc changelog:changelog (CHANGELOG.md) is missing`
   `blocking · schema-conformance.home-vacated — … route: restore the document at 'CHANGELOG.md' and commit it — 'git log --diff-filter=D -1 -- CHANGELOG.md' names the commit that removed it — then 'jigc ingest' to re-register it`
Running the emitted locator verbatim in that repo prints **nothing** (exit 0, empty stdout) — there is no removing commit, because the deletion is not committed. The act that actually repairs the state, `git checkout -- CHANGELOG.md`, is named by neither row, and `jigc ingest` re-registers nothing while the file is absent. This is the *"a route that, followed exactly, changes nothing"* shape the same function's doc-comment cites M46's PT-1 for, reintroduced in the sibling cell.

CLASS, AND HOW THE COUNT WAS DERIVED: `grep -rn "diff-filter=D" crates` → **1 hit**, `crates/cli/src/orphan.rs:632`, the only production producer of this clause. One site; the duplicate-blocking-row half is a consequence of that one producer not discriminating the committed from the uncommitted cell.

summary: The M52 deliverable substantially holds. I drove the wave's headline classes through the real binary and every one behaved as claimed: the nine-member posture family refuses and routes correctly (squash-merge driven), all nine `milestone` doors refuse a repo with no `jigc setup` and write nothing, the destroying doors refuse/narrate/displace over foreign bytes (`task discard`, `milestone discard`, `uninstall`, and `task finalize`'s `.jigc/displaced/<id>/` move with the always-present `displaced` envelope key), a racing `pre-commit` hook that writes into a freshly minted working area has its prose preserved and named by `milestone.foreign-bytes`, verb-routed workflows refuse at both compose doors and are gone from the `jigc start` catalog, the fixed-identity guard answers at every address door ahead of the grammar and ceiling checks, and a hook-rejected `--format json` finalize emits exactly one parseable document on stderr with stdout empty. `dev/gate` is green: 3785 passed / 0 failed, fmt + clippy clean. The one headline concern is a new exit-flipping check that fires outside the state it was designed for: `schema-conformance.home-vacated` keys on *any* history at a declared home, so an ordinary brownfield repo that once had a `CHANGELOG.md` (or `VISION.md`, or `docs/roadmap.md`) is blocking-red at `jigc validate` exit 1 the moment `jigc setup` runs — a measured regression against rc.15 with no route that clears it — and its acceptance suite cannot see it, because all four arms build an already-adopted corpus and the never-adopted state has no fixture in the Rust suites at all.
